description: Single declarative host adapter registry (SRC-028:R008). Every consumer -- tools/saipen_engine/admission.py, bootstrap/inject.ps1, bootstrap/inject.sh, tools/autoinject.py, status/freshness reporting and the parity tests -- reads host identity, install surfaces and enforcement capability from THIS file. No consumer may keep a second handwritten host inventory. declared_strength is what the adapter CLAIMS for an installed, current, healthy install; effective enforcement is computed at runtime by admission.effective_strength and is never stronger than the installed state proves. `response_enforcement` is a SEPARATE claim about the FINAL-RESPONSE contract only (EXEC-RESPONSE-01), never derived from `declared_strength`: MECHANICAL means a completed-part hook can replace/refuse model text or a post-render Stop hook can request one correction; it never implies invisible pre-stream prevention, ADVISORY means the contract reaches the model as instructions only, UNAVAILABLE means the host has no final-response surface at all. A host may claim MECHANICAL only with a `response_hook` token its own `hook_artifact` actually contains, and host-level trust evidence stays separate from the capability claim.

adapters.name: OpenCode
adapters.hook_surface_note: The supported runtime's global local plugin directory is the PLURAL `plugins/` (OpenCode 1.18.x `opencode debug config` reports a plugin origin for it and instantiates the factory). The singular `plugin/` directory is ALSO discovered by the same runtime, so a stale copy there would load this hook a second time: the injectors remove the legacy surface on install and uninstall removes both. EXEC-RESPONSE-01 checks completed text parts through experimental.text.complete; this V1 hook is not a token-stream gate and has no direct V2 migration equivalent.
adapters.routine_launch: generic OpenCode launch; no SAIPEN seat required
adapters.response_enforcement_note: Default operational completed parts are replaced by the canonical machine digest; oversized model text is not the delivered completed part, and a refused part is handed to `saipen response preserve` before it is replaced, so it is kept byte for byte with its overflow account. This is not a token-stream gate; previously streamed text and intermediate narration cannot be retracted. Explicit witnessed depth/artifacts remain separately gated.
adapters.prelaunch_contract: ok+RUNTIME_CURRENT|RUNTIME_RESYNCED admits a host start; every other code refuses it. The supported launch invokes this before the host process exists (saipen/RUNTIME.md).
adapters.admission_enforcement_note: ADVISORY: the plugin admits tools against the project binding (a different boundary) and gates completed text parts, but it writes no protocol-admission evidence, so admission stays ADVISORY while chat style is measured at the same surface (T-1568: an unreadable or unclassifiable authority is passed, not refused, so this is measurement and never hard admission).
adapters.execution_capability_note: EXECUTION.md instructs silent tool continuation. No supported pre-render intermediate-text interception is installed; final/Stop hooks cannot retract streamed text. Machine progress uses canonical status and runtime heartbeat. Native thought UI is host-owned. Higher-priority host narration requirements take precedence and prevent a silence guarantee.
adapters.degraded_mode_note: No prompt-level admission hook exists. The consequential tool gate applies the operator policy for a missing guard, unavailable interpreter or replaced loaded plugin: DEGRADED_ALLOWED permits the tool with a bounded UNVERIFIED system record, and a replaced plugin whose guard still answers keeps that guard's target and actor refusals; STRICT refuses with the taxonomy action. Missing policy uses the canonical default, invalid policy uses STRICT. Known forged or foreign binding and normal guard refusals still block in every mode. Decisions are compiled from HOST-INTEGRATION-01 and checked against its owner.
adapters.question_enforcement_note: OPERATOR-QUESTION-01: capability only; installed generation and actual hook execution remain separate evidence. Canonical status/response owns human eligibility; no typed canonical choices means no improvised menu.

adapters.name: Claude Code
adapters.hook_surface_note: Executable native Claude Code transport for PROTOCOL-ADMISSION-01 and the layered final-response gate (T-1558). ONE artifact dispatches on `hook_event_name`: SessionStart (drop the record and deliver again, one engine call), UserPromptSubmit (the pre-generation boundary: establish admission and deliver BOTH BOOT/STYLE/EXECUTION and the generated chat contract; a runtime REFUSAL blocks the prompt with a runtime-written diagnostic and its one operator action; a DEGRADED permit proceeds, marked UNVERIFIED for operator and model), PostToolUse on Bash (a real `saipen init` binds the SAME turn), PostModelSwitch (invalidate), Stop (forward `last_assistant_message` to `tools/saipen.py response check --classify --admission-session`, the SAME authority the Codex and OpenCode gates use). The hook holds exactly one rule of its own (T-1624): an engine that cannot be run is ENGINE_UNREACHABLE, which lets the prompt through with a plain notice under the default policy and blocks only under STRICT. The command names the host's INSTALLED runtime (`hook_delegate`), never the source checkout, and is POSIX-spelled (forward slashes) because Claude Code runs hooks through Git Bash on Windows. The installer stages the artifact, proves it starts, stays silent outside a project and fails open without a runtime, and only then activates it; the previous generation is kept for `--rollback`. It merges into the operator's shared settings.json, preserves every unrelated hook, and REPORTS (never removes) an operator hook that carries its own voice or language rule (`style_hook_conflicts`).
adapters.response_enforcement_note: The Stop event supplies the outgoing final message and one correction continuation is enforced for operational boundaries AND for ordinary chat that breaks the measurable STYLE.md contract (CHAT_STYLE_DRIFT). SEPARATE EVIDENCE, not part of this claim: a stop that is already a continuation records CLAUDE_STOP_REENTRY_NO_FAIL_CLOSED rather than closing fail-closed, and the hook is inert until installed (`python tools/install_host_guard.py claude`). POST-RENDER: text already exists and may already be visible; no retraction or hard invisible prevention. Each fresh Stop gets the same canonical gate; re-entry remains one correction, not fail-closed.
adapters.admission_enforcement_note: MECHANICAL, through a separated host authority (T-1623, hardened T-1624): the hook mints nothing. It asks the SAIPEN host-authority broker (`saipen_engine/host_authority_broker.py`), which runs as its own process, keeps its signing key in memory only, and admits exactly one caller shape proven from the operating system (`saipen_engine/host_authority_identity.py`): a host image that carries the registered code signer, shells that were started to run exactly the hook command, and the shipped hook bytes declaring this host. A descendant of the host that is not that invocation -- a command the model runs through the shell tool, a direct CLI call, a module import -- is refused, as is an interpreter renamed after the host. The broker mints a short-lived capability bound to the host adapter, project, session, model, provider, authority fingerprints and generation, and owns the ledger write. T-1563 still holds for everything else: project keys, importable signing helpers, environment strings, prompt text and legacy `hook:<event>:<mac>` values prove nothing. MECHANICAL is the claim for a session the broker ADMITTED; a session it could not prove runs DEGRADED under the default policy and is reported as such, never as admitted. Known limits, recorded rather than hidden: the proof is what the OS reports about live processes, so it is not a boundary against code injected into the host process, a same-user process that rewrites the installed hook, or a forged parent; the code-signer check exists on Windows only, and a platform that does not report process identity (no /proc) has no mechanical admission at all.

adapters.name: Codex CLI
adapters.hook_surface_note: Executable native Codex Stop transport for the canonical EXEC-RESPONSE-01 gate (T-1551): the hook forwards the Stop event's `last_assistant_message` to `tools/saipen.py response check --classify` -- the SAME renderer/checker OpenCode's text gate uses -- and maps the verdict onto Codex hook output. No response schema lives in the adapter. The Stop gate enforces by requiring a correction continuation; it never retracts rendered text. Re-entry is bounded deliberately: the first invalid stop of a turn requests exactly one correction, and a stop that is already a Stop-hook continuation (`stop_hook_active`) records the exact capability boundary CODEX_STOP_REENTRY_NO_FAIL_CLOSED instead of looping. Trust is an external host boundary: Codex skips non-managed hooks until the operator reviews and trusts the hash-bound definition via /hooks, and installing never marks a hook trusted. CODEX_STOP_TEXT_CLASSIFICATION: the Stop event carries no turn ingress or tool context, so a markerless reply on an idle turn is indistinguishable from ordinary chat and passes.
adapters.response_enforcement_note: The supported Stop event supplies the outgoing final message and one correction continuation is enforced. SEPARATE EVIDENCE, not part of this claim: the hook requires host trust, and a Stop that is already a continuation records CODEX_STOP_REENTRY_NO_FAIL_CLOSED rather than closing fail-closed. POST-RENDER: text already exists and may already be visible; no retraction or hard invisible prevention. Each fresh Stop gets the same canonical gate; re-entry remains one correction, not fail-closed.
adapters.admission_enforcement_note: UNAVAILABLE: the shipped Codex transport is a Stop hook only. It has no delivery hook and no pre-output boundary, so it cannot observe that authority reached the model and cannot stop a reply before it exists. The admission layer is reported NOT_ENFORCEABLE for this host, never passed as admitted.

adapters.name: ZAICODE
adapters.home_note: ZAICODE runs with an isolated HOME (<workspace>/.zaicode/home) and never shares ~/.zcode with a production ZCode; ZAICODE_HOME names that HOME, and an unset variable means ZAICODE is not configured on this machine.
adapters.hook_surface_note: ZAICODE loads this process hook from ~/.zcode/cli/config.json and runs it as argv with shell:false, which is why the installer writes it with HOOK_BOOTSTRAP and the broker's max_shells:0 policy. The SKILL and instruction surfaces stay inside ZAICODE_HOME (the isolated home); the hook config is the operator profile's ~/.zcode because that is the file the running host reads. Without this declaration the canonical injector skipped the hook step entirely and runtime_bootstrap.hook_problems answered [] at any drift, so a repaired artifact never reached the operator (T-1934/T-1935).

operator_ingress_capability.provenance_transport_note: SPECIFIED, NOT INSTALLED (T-1823 review of SRC-277/T-1818). The two carrier mechanisms -- SAIPEN_TASK_FILE/SAIPEN_TASK_SHA256 exported by the tool-process spawner, or .saipen/cache/ingress/ envelopes written on operator input -- are a FreeBuff-side obligation that has NOT been implemented or observed: T-1822 measured live that a genuine operator 'cc' typed in the FreeBuff UI reaches the engine with no SAIPEN_TASK_FILE, no SAIPEN_TASK_SHA256 and no host ingress envelope, so its witness is model_supplied and operator_required hard_wait correctly refuses it. This registry records installed, verified host behaviour; it must stay at host_prompt_available false / prompt_to_work_binding NOT_INSTALLED / no supported carrier until a real FreeBuff-launched tool process delivers a carrier that host-to-engine acceptance can verify. SAIPEN cannot and must not manufacture that carrier itself.
